Because the regularized objective need not be a lower bound, compute certification from the unregularized value \(q_k=\min\{\eta:(z,\eta)\in M_k\}\), not from the stabilized selection objective.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Outer Approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratically stabilized OA centered at a reference master point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_k\) be the current OA master and \(\bar z^k\) a reference point. For \(\rho_k>0\), choose \((z^k,\eta^k)\) by solving \(\min\{\eta+\tfrac{\rho_k}{2}\|z-\bar z^k\|_2^2:(z,\eta)\in M_k\}\). Solve the continuous subproblem associated with the discrete part of \(z^k\), add valid supporting or feasibility cuts, and move \(\bar z^k\) after a prescribed improvement; otherwise retain the center. Use the unpenalized master optimum for the global lower bound, and stop only by a certified original-objective gap or exhaustive assignment treatment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proximal OA selects nearby master candidates using a quadratic penalty while certifying progress with the original, unpenalized master objective.

knowledge_statements.title: Stabilization Parameter Regimes

A vanishing regime \(\rho_k\to0\) is additionally suitable when asymptotic recovery of unregularized master minimizers is required. Negative parameters or termination from the penalized value are inadmissible.

knowledge_statements.title: Interior-Point Outer-Approximation Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Error-corrected supporting cuts generated from exact or approximate interior continuous points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be convex, let \(\phi:D\to\mathbb R\) be convex, and let \(\bar z\in\operatorname{ri}D\). Suppose \(\widetilde g\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\Delta\ge 0\) satisfy \(\phi(\bar z)+\widetilde g^{\mathsf T}(z-\bar z)-\Delta\le\phi(z)\) for every \(z\in D\). Then \(\ell(z)=\phi(\bar z)+\widetilde g^{\mathsf T}(z-\bar z)-\Delta\) is a global affine minorant, and \(\ell(z)\le 0\) is a valid outer relaxation of \(\phi(z)\le 0\). If \(\phi\) is differentiable at \(\bar z\), the exact-gradient choice is \(\widetilde g=\nabla\phi(\bar z)\) and \(\Delta=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An interior continuous solver can provide a valid OA cut through an exact gradient at a differentiability point or through an approximate affine minorant whose global error correction is certified.

children.title: Relaxation-Point Separation

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Point Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: ECP linearization of nonlinear constraints violated at the current relaxation solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a polyhedral relaxation containing the linear constraints and variable domains. At iteration \(k\), solve it to obtain \(z^k\). For every selected differentiable convex constraint \(g_j(z)\le0\) with \(g_j(z^k)>\varepsilon_j\), add the supporting cut \(g_j(z^k)+\nabla g_j(z^k)^{\mathsf T}(z-z^k)\le0\). Reoptimize the augmented relaxation and repeat. If no selected constraint is violated beyond tolerance and \(z^k\) satisfies the integrality and certified-gap tests, return \(z^k\); otherwise continue separation or branching according to the encompassing ECP scheme.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: ECP repeatedly linearizes violated convex constraints at the current relaxation solution and reoptimizes until feasibility, integrality, and bound tests are satisfied.
assumptions_latex: Each \(g_j\) is differentiable and convex on the relaxation domain.
Every added tangent inequality is retained as a valid global cut.
Relaxation solves provide valid bounds.

children.title: Constraint-Selection Families

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Selection Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: ECP policies for choosing a separating subset of currently violated nonlinear constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At relaxation point \(z^k\), form \(V_k=\{j:g_j(z^k)>\varepsilon_j\}\). An all-violated policy selects \(S_k=V_k\); a maximum-violation policy selects any \(j_k\in\arg\max_{j\in V_k}g_j(z^k)/s_j\) and sets \(S_k=\{j_k\}\); a threshold policy selects \(S_k=\{j\in V_k:g_j(z^k)/s_j\ge\theta\max_{i\in V_k}g_i(z^k)/s_i\}\), where \(s_j>0\) and \(0<\theta\le1\). Add a valid supporting cut for every \(j\in S_k\). For convergence, the policy must not indefinitely ignore any persistently violated constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: ECP may cut all violations, only the largest scaled violation, or a threshold subset, provided persistently violated constraints are eventually selected.
assumptions_latex: Each selected constraint admits a valid supporting cut at \(z^k\).
\(s_j>0\) and \(0<\theta\le1\).
Persistent violations are selected after finitely many subsequent iterations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The policy generates at least one separating cut whenever \(V_k\ne\varnothing\) and preserves convergence fairness.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a master candidate \(w^k\), select a cut point \(z^k\) by one of four rules: use \(w^k\) itself, project \(w^k\) onto a designated convex set, repair it through a continuous feasibility problem, or interpolate it with an interior reference point. For every selected violated constraint, append

\]

children.title: Convex Global-Convergence Regime
children.top_down_role: The classical globally convergent convex MINLP regime.

assumptions_latex: The continuous domain is compact and convex, the discrete domain is finite, and all subproblems and master problems are solved exactly.
The objective and nonlinear constraints are continuous and convex in the continuous variables for each fixed discrete assignment.

notation.meaning: master lower bound at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical exact convex-MINLP convergence regime for a cut-retaining ECP scheme.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider an ECP sequence whose master relaxations contain only globally valid supporting cuts. Then \(L_k\le v^*\le U_k\), the sequence \((L_k)\) is nondecreasing, and \((U_k)\) is nonincreasing whenever incumbents improve. If infinitely many iterations occur, compactness provides accumulation points; exact separation and continuity ensure that any accumulation point not satisfying the nonlinear constraints produces a persistent violated cut. Consequently, every accepted feasible accumulation point with vanishing bound gap is globally optimal, and
\[
\lim_{k\to\infty}L_k=\lim_{k\to\infty}U_k=v^*.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under compactness, convexity, exact solves, valid separation, and retained cuts, ECP bounds converge to the global optimum and feasible limit points are globally optimal.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the master with any subset of \(\mathcal C\). At an infeasible master solution, add a violated inequality from \(\mathcal C\); at a feasible solution, accept it if the master objective meets the incumbent bound. Because an inequality already present cannot be violated by a master-feasible solution, every unsuccessful iteration adds a distinct member of \(\mathcal C\). Hence no more than \(|\mathcal C|\) additions are possible. Once no violated member remains, the master feasible set equals the original feasible set over its domain, so a globally solved master yields a global optimum or an infeasibility declaration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If finitely many valid cuts exactly describe feasibility and each failed iteration adds a new one, ECP closes after at most that many additions.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Closure Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The abstract finite-closure bound is plausible and complexity_bound fits the leaf, but no source supports this specialization and the statement contains proof-style reasoning that must be removed in a sourced revision.

children.title: Tolerance-Based Termination Regime
children.top_down_role: Practical completion governed by violation and bound tolerances.

assumptions_latex: The master value \(L_k\) is a valid global lower bound and the incumbent value \(U_k\) comes from a point satisfying the required integrality restrictions.
Constraint and objective scales are fixed before applying tolerances.
The tolerances \(\varepsilon_f,\varepsilon_a,\varepsilon_r\) are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned incumbent has maximum recorded violation at most \(\varepsilon_f\) and certified bound gap at most \(\varepsilon_a+\varepsilon_r\max\{1,|U_k|\}\).

notation.meaning: current valid lower and incumbent upper bounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Practical stopping certificate with separately stated feasibility and objective-gap tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For incumbent \((x^k,y^k)\), define
\[
r_k=\max_i\max\{g_i(x^k,y^k),0\},\qquad
\Delta_k=U_k-L_k.
\]
Terminate when
\[
r_k\le\varepsilon_f
\quad\text{and}\quad
\Delta_k\le\varepsilon_a+\varepsilon_r\max\{1,|U_k|\}.
\]
Output the incumbent, \(L_k\), \(U_k\), \(r_k\), and \(\Delta_k\). If \(\varepsilon_f=0\), the incumbent is feasible for the original constraints and \(U_k-v^*\le\Delta_k\). If \(\varepsilon_f>0\), the record certifies only tolerance-feasibility unless an additional repair or error-bound argument converts it to exact feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop when both maximum constraint violation and the certified lower-to-upper bound gap meet specified tolerances; positive feasibility tolerance alone does not prove exact feasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance-Based Termination Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stopping certificate is mathematically plausible, but g_i, its index set, and the scope of recorded violations are not fully introduced. The particular absolute-relative gap convention also lacks a source.

children.title: Nonconvex ECP Extension Boundary
children.top_down_role: Extensions whose global guarantees require additional structure beyond convex MINLP.

assumptions_latex: ECP applies the convex first-order cut formula to a differentiable constraint without a global convex underestimator.
No independent global-validity test or spatial partition restricts the cut.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For nonconvex constraints, a tangent inequality can exclude feasible points; classical convex ECP global guarantees therefore do not extend without additional structure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of tangent-cut validity after removing convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the nonconvex constraint
\[
g(x)=1-x^2\le 0,
\]
whose feasible set is \(( -\infty,-1]\cup[1,\infty )\). Linearization at \(z=0\) gives
\[
g(0)+g'(0)(x-0)=1\le 0,
\]
which is impossible and therefore removes every feasible point, including \(x=1\). Thus the tangent inequality used by convex ECP is not generally a relaxation when convexity is absent. A nonconvex extension requires globally valid underestimators, domain partitioning, convexification, or another mechanism that independently establishes cut validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without convexity, an ECP tangent can remove genuine feasible points; global convergence requires valid underestimators, partitioning, convexification, or comparable extra structure.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex ECP Extension Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample correctly demonstrates failure of tangent-cut validity without convexity, and failure_boundary is the correct kind, but the record supplies no admissible evidence or standard-field rationale.

children.title: Generalized Benders Decomposition for Convex MINLP
children.top_down_role: Projection-based decomposition using continuous-subproblem value and feasibility certificates in a discrete master space.

children.title: Generalized Benders Projection Architecture
children.top_down_role: Elimination of continuous variables through parametric value and feasibility information.

children.title: Generalized Benders Primal Subproblem Family
children.top_down_role: Continuous convex subproblems parameterized by master decisions.

assumptions_latex: The master parameter belongs to a set \(Y\), and \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a nonempty closed convex continuous domain.
For every fixed \(y\in Y\), the functions \(f(\cdot,y)\) and \(g_i(\cdot,y)\) are proper convex functions on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The parameterized primal subproblem defines either the projected value \(\phi(y)\) or an infeasibility outcome used to construct a master certificate.

notation.meaning: continuous feasible set at parameter y

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-master-variable continuous convex subproblem used by generalized Benders decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each master decision \(y\in Y\), the generalized Benders primal subproblem is
\[
\phi(y)=\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x,y):g_i(x,y)\le0,
\ i=1,\ldots,m\}.
\]
If \(F(y)\neq\varnothing\) and the infimum is attained, a minimizer \(x(y)\) and associated dual information generate projected optimality information. If \(F(y)=\varnothing\), an auxiliary convex feasibility subproblem is solved to generate projected exclusion information. Thus the family is indexed by master decisions while optimization within each member is exclusively over the continuous variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixing a master decision yields a continuous convex optimization problem whose value or infeasibility information is projected back into the discrete master.
knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Benders Primal Subproblem Family

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The parameterized convex subproblem definition fits the container, but the generalized Benders formulation and the asserted auxiliary feasibility-subproblem response have no cited source.

children.title: Generalized Benders Projected Masters
children.top_down_role: Discrete masters representing projected value and feasibility information.

assumptions_latex: Each feasible primal subproblem satisfies strong duality, and each infeasible parameter admits a valid feasibility certificate.
All cuts retained by the master are global lower bounds or valid exclusions over \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projected master is a relaxation of the original problem, and becomes exact when all valid optimality and feasibility certificates are imposed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph master assembled from dual lower bounds and projected feasibility exclusions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For collected dual multipliers \(\Lambda_k\) and accumulated feasibility exclusions, a generalized Benders master has the form
\[
\min_{y\in Y,\eta}\ \eta
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
\eta\ge q(y,\lambda)\ \text{for all }\lambda\in\Lambda_k,
\quad y\notin Y_{\mathrm{cut}}.
\]
Every optimality inequality underestimates \(\phi(y)\), and every feasibility constraint removes only parameters whose continuous subproblem is infeasible. Hence its optimum is a lower bound on the original optimum. With the complete families of valid optimality and feasibility certificates, its feasible epigraph equals the projection of the original problem's feasible epigraph onto \((y,\eta)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The projected master minimizes an epigraph variable over discrete decisions using dual lower bounds and valid exclusions; the complete certificate family gives the exact projection.
knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Benders Projected Masters

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is the correct kind, but y notin Y_cut does not specify the actual projected feasibility inequalities. Exactness of the complete master also requires a sourced theorem with precise duality and completeness conditions.

children.title: Generalized Benders Certificate Families
children.top_down_role: Master information separated according to feasible and infeasible continuous subproblems.

children.title: Generalized Benders Optimality Certificates
children.top_down_role: Projected value information obtained from feasible convex subproblems.

assumptions_latex: At \(\bar y\), the primal subproblem is feasible, attains its optimum, and satisfies strong duality.
A dual optimum \(\bar\lambda\ge0\) is attained, and \(q(y,\bar\lambda)\) is evaluable for every master decision \(y\in Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality \(\eta\ge q(y,\bar\lambda)\) is globally valid and is exact at \(y=\bar y\).

notation.meaning: optimal multiplier at the sampled parameter

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual optimality certificate from a feasible, strongly dual convex subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Weak duality gives
\[
q(y,\bar\lambda)\le\phi(y)
\quad\text{for every }y\in Y.
\]
Therefore the master inequality
\[
\eta\ge q(y,\bar\lambda)
\]
is a verifiable global lower bound on the projected value function. Strong duality and dual attainment at the sampled parameter imply
\[
q(\bar y,\bar\lambda)=\phi(\bar y),
\]
so the certificate is tight at \(\bar y\). Verification consists of checking dual feasibility of \(\bar\lambda\), computing the infimum defining \(q\), and confirming equality with the attained primal value at \(\bar y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An attained optimal multiplier yields a dual lower-bound cut valid for every master decision and tight at the sampled feasible decision.
knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Benders Optimality Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Under the stated strong-duality and attainment assumptions, the optimality certificate is mathematically coherent and correctly typed, but no source supports the generalized Benders cut formulation.

children.title: Generalized Benders Feasibility Certificates
children.top_down_role: Projected exclusion information obtained from infeasible convex subproblems.

assumptions_latex: For a sampled parameter \(\bar y\), the set \(\{x\in X:g_i(x,\bar y)\le0\ \forall i\}\) is empty.
The auxiliary minimax feasibility problem and its dual attain equal values.
The functions \(g_i(\cdot,y)\) are convex on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A multiplier \(\bar\lambda\ge0\) with \(\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}\bar\lambda=1\) and positive dual value certifies infeasibility and yields a valid projected exclusion.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized-dual certificate obtained from a convex minimum-violation subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Solve
\[
\rho(\bar y)=\inf_{x\in X,u}\{u:g_i(x,\bar y)\le u,
\ i=1,\ldots,m\}.
\]
Infeasibility of the original subproblem is certified when \(\rho(\bar y)>0\). Under the stated alternative, there exists \(\bar\lambda\ge0\) with \(\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}\bar\lambda=1\) such that
\[
h(\bar y,\bar\lambda)=
\inf_{x\in X}\bar\lambda^{\mathsf T}g(x,\bar y)=
\rho(\bar y)>0.
\]
Any parameter \(y\) satisfying \(h(y,\bar\lambda)>0\) is infeasible, so the projected master may impose \(h(y,\bar\lambda)\le0\) without excluding any feasible parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive minimum-violation value and normalized dual multiplier certify subproblem infeasibility and generate a master constraint excluding only infeasible parameters.
knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Benders Feasibility Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The normalized minimax certificate is plausible under the stated attainment and equality assumptions, but those assumptions and the resulting projected exclusion require a specific source.

children.title: Generalized Benders Validity Condition
children.top_down_role: Duality, regularity, and value-function regimes supporting globally valid projected information.

children.title: Strong-Duality Regime
children.top_down_role: Convex subproblem regimes where dual information provides exact projected certificates.

assumptions_latex: For fixed \(\bar y\), the primal subproblem is convex, has finite value, and possesses a point \(x^s\in\operatorname{ri}X\) with \(g_i(x^s,\bar y)<0\) for every inequality.
The objective and constraints are proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions of the continuous variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal and Lagrangian-dual values coincide; under dual attainment, an optimal multiplier supplies an exact projected optimality certificate at \(\bar y\).

notation.meaning: primal projected value at the fixed parameter

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex inequality subproblem under a relative-interior Slater condition.

source_refs.locator: 2.12.2 Saddle Point of a Function p. 75

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
q(\bar y,\lambda)=
\inf_{x\in X}\bigl(f(x,\bar y)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}g(x,\bar y)\bigr),
\qquad \lambda\ge0.
\]
The Slater condition implies zero duality gap:
\[
\phi(\bar y)=\sup_{\lambda\ge0}q(\bar y,\lambda).
\]
If the dual supremum is attained at \(\bar\lambda\), then \(q(\bar y,\bar\lambda)=\phi(\bar y)\). Thus the dual function is not merely a lower bound at the sampled master decision; it gives exact projected value information there and supports a tight generalized Benders optimality cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Slater regularity gives equality of primal and dual subproblem values; an attained dual optimum therefore produces an exact projected value certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong-Duality Regime

source_witnesses.locator: 2.12.2 Saddle Point of a Function p. 75

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The local file exposes only a table-of-contents entry for the cited saddle-point section. Moreover, a relative-interior Slater condition must be stated relative to the effective domains of the objective and constraints, not merely ri X, before the zero-gap claim is reliable.

children.title: Value-Function Support Regime
children.top_down_role: Parametric regimes admitting valid supporting master information.

assumptions_latex: The parameter domain \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^p\) is convex, and the projected value function \(\phi:D\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper convex.
The sampled parameter \(\bar y\) lies in \(\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}\phi)\), so \(\partial\phi(\bar y)\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(s\in\partial\phi(\bar y)\) defines a globally valid affine master support that is exact at \(\bar y\).

notation.meaning: subgradient of the value function at the sampled parameter

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex value-function support on a continuous parameter domain containing the master decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
By the definition of a convex subgradient, every \(s\in\partial\phi(\bar y)\) satisfies
\[
\phi(y)\ge
\phi(\bar y)+s^{\mathsf T}(y-\bar y)
\quad\text{for all }y\in D.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\eta\ge
\phi(\bar y)+s^{\mathsf T}(y-\bar y)
\]
is a valid projected master inequality, including when the master searches only over \(Y\subseteq D\). Equality holds at \(y=\bar y\). In generalized Benders decomposition, an attained primal-dual solution may provide such a subgradient through multiplier sensitivity, provided the required parametric regularity holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subgradient of a convex projected value function supplies a globally valid affine lower support, tight at the sampled master decision.
knowledge_statements.title: Value-Function Support Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The subgradient support inequality is correct for a proper convex value function and property fits the leaf. However, no source is supplied, particularly for the claim that generalized Benders primal-dual solutions provide such subgradients under parametric regularity.

children.title: Infeasibility-Alternative Regime
children.top_down_role: Regularity regimes providing projected infeasibility certificates.

assumptions_latex: The auxiliary violation value is \(\rho(y)=\inf_{x\in X}\max_i g_i(x,y)\), with the infimum attained.
A convex minimax theorem or equivalent constraint qualification gives \(\rho(y)=\sup_{\lambda\in\Delta_m}\inf_{x\in X}\lambda^{\mathsf T}g(x,y)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The continuous subproblem is infeasible exactly when some normalized nonnegative multiplier has strictly positive dual value.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimax alternative for inequality feasibility with simplex-normalized multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the stated minimax equality,
\[
\rho(y)=\sup_{\lambda\in\Delta_m}h(y,\lambda),
\qquad
h(y,\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}\lambda^{\mathsf T}g(x,y).
\]
The system \(g_i(x,y)\le0\) for all \(i\) is feasible if and only if \(\rho(y)\le0\). Therefore it is infeasible if and only if
\[
\rho(y)>0,
\]
and, when the dual supremum is attained, this is equivalent to the existence of \(\bar\lambda\in\Delta_m\) satisfying \(h(y,\bar\lambda)>0\). Such a multiplier is a finite projected infeasibility certificate and supports the valid master condition \(h(y,\bar\lambda)\le0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under an attained minimax alternative, infeasibility is equivalent to a normalized nonnegative multiplier whose weighted constraint infimum is strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.title: Infeasibility-Alternative Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The equivalence is coherent when primal attainment, minimax equality, and dual attainment hold, and duality fits the regime container. A source is required to establish the precise regularity conditions yielding that alternative.

children.title: Primal-Dual Attainment Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Cases where available dual information does not provide exact projected certificates.

children.title: Duality-Gap Failures
children.top_down_role: Subproblem regimes where dual information does not recover the projected primal value.

knowledge_statements.title: Duality-Gap Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive Lagrangian duality gap in a fixed-integer convex subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(Y\subseteq\mathbb Z^p\), \(f:X\times Y\to\mathbb R\), and \(g:X\times Y\to\mathbb R^m\). For fixed \(y\in Y\), define \(v(y)=\inf\{f(x,y):x\in X,\ g(x,y)\le 0\}\), \(L(x,\lambda;y)=f(x,y)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}g(x,y)\), and \(d(y)=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m}\inf_{x\in X}L(x,\lambda;y)\). Weak duality gives \(d(y)\le v(y)\). A duality-gap failure occurs when \(v(y)\in\mathbb R\) and \(d(y)<v(y)\). Then every lower certificate obtained from a multiplier \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\) has value at most \(d(y)\) at this fixed \(y\), so no such certificate is exact there. Consequently, generalized Benders exactness at \(y\) cannot be obtained solely from this multiplier-certificate family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive gap between a fixed subproblem's primal and Lagrangian-dual values prevents any certificate from that multiplier family from reproducing the primal value at the fixed point.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty and convex, and \(Y\subseteq\mathbb Z^p\).
For each fixed \(y\in Y\), \(f(\cdot,y)\) and every component \(g_i(\cdot,y)\) are convex on \(X\).
\(v(y)\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d(y)<v(y)\Longrightarrow\) no certificate from the stated multiplier family is exact at \(y\).

notation.meaning: primal value of the fixed-integer subproblem

children.title: Primal Attainment Failures
children.top_down_role: Cases where the relevant primal value is approached but no optimizer is attained.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Attainment Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite fixed-integer subproblem value not achieved by any continuous solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(Y\subseteq\mathbb Z^p\), \(f:X\times Y\to\mathbb R\), and \(g:X\times Y\to\mathbb R^m\). For fixed \(y\in Y\), define \(F(y)=\{x\in X:g(x,y)\le0\}\) and \(v(y)=\inf_{x\in F(y)}f(x,y)\). Primal attainment fails when \(F(y)\ne\varnothing\), \(v(y)\in\mathbb R\), and \(f(x,y)>v(y)\) for every \(x\in F(y)\). A minimizing sequence with objective values converging to \(v(y)\) exists, but no feasible point attains that value. Consequently, a generalized Benders construction that requires an optimal primal point cannot form its point-based certificate at \(y\), even if the dual value equals \(v(y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The fixed subproblem has a finite infimum but no feasible optimizer, so a Benders construction requiring an optimal primal point cannot form its point-based certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(Y\subseteq\mathbb Z^p\), \(f:X\times Y\to\mathbb R\), and \(g:X\times Y\to\mathbb R^m\).
\(F(y)\ne\varnothing\).
\(v(y)\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F(y)}f(x,y)=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: continuous feasible set at the fixed integer vector

children.title: Dual Attainment Failures
children.top_down_role: Cases where exact multiplier certificates are unavailable through attained dual solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Attainment Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact dual value approached but not achieved by a multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(Y\subseteq\mathbb Z^p\), \(f:X\times Y\to\mathbb R\), and \(g:X\times Y\to\mathbb R^m\). For fixed \(y\in Y\), define \(q(\lambda;y)=\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x,y)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}g(x,y)\}\) for \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\), and let \(d(y)=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m}q(\lambda;y)\). Dual attainment fails when \(d(y)\in\mathbb R\) but \(q(\lambda;y)<d(y)\) for every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\). Even if strong duality gives \(d(y)=v(y)\), no optimal multiplier exists, so an exact generalized Benders certificate indexed by a dual optimizer is unavailable. There nevertheless exists a sequence \((\lambda^k)\subseteq\mathbb R_+^m\) for which \(q(\lambda^k;y)\to d(y)\), yielding multiplier certificates that approach the dual value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual supremum is finite and may equal the primal value, but no multiplier attains it; certificates from multipliers can approach, but cannot attain, the exact value.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(Y\subseteq\mathbb Z^p\), \(f:X\times Y\to\mathbb R\), and \(g:X\times Y\to\mathbb R^m\).
The dual function \(q(\cdot;y)\) is well-defined on \(\mathbb R_+^m\).
\(d(y)\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmax}_{\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m}q(\lambda;y)=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: dual function at the fixed integer vector

children.title: Projected-Certificate Breakdown
children.top_down_role: Consequences of duality or attainment failure for generalized Benders information.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected-Certificate Breakdown
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of attained dual certificates to represent the projected value function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v(y)=\inf\{f(x,y):x\in X,\ g(x,y)\le0\}\), and let each available dual certificate define a valid lower function \(\ell_\lambda(y)\le v(y)\). Projected-certificate exactness at \(\bar y\) requires some admissible \(\bar\lambda\) satisfying \(\ell_{\bar\lambda}(\bar y)=v(\bar y)\). Breakdown occurs if \(v(\bar y)\in\mathbb R\) but \(\sup_\lambda\ell_\lambda(\bar y)<v(\bar y)\), or if equality holds only as an unattained supremum. In either case no single available projected cut supports the value-function epigraph at \((\bar y,v(\bar y))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected cuts fail when no available dual certificate attains the subproblem value at the evaluated integer point.
assumptions_latex: Every \(\ell_\lambda\) is a globally valid lower bound for \(v\).
\(v(\bar y)\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nexists\bar\lambda:\ell_{\bar\lambda}(\bar y)=v(\bar y)\).

notation.meaning: lower function induced by a dual certificate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind and mathematical distinction are plausible, but no source identifies the admissible certificate family or supports the asserted connection to projected generalized Benders cuts.

children.title: Generalized Benders Variants
children.top_down_role: Variants distinguished by aggregation, stabilization, and certificate source.

children.title: Generalized Benders Cut-Granularity Family
children.top_down_role: Aggregated and disaggregated projected-master architectures.

children.title: Single-Cut Generalized Benders
children.top_down_role: Projected-master architectures using aggregated subproblem information.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Cut Generalized Benders
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregate-cut variant for a separable convex subproblem value function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v(y)=\sum_{s=1}^S v_s(y)\) on a mixed-integer master set \(Y\). Initialize \(C_0=\varnothing\). At iteration \(k\), solve \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}y+\theta:y\in Y,\ \theta\ge\alpha_j+\beta_j^{\mathsf T}y\ (j\in C_k)\}\), obtaining \(y^k\). Solve every convex subproblem and obtain valid component lower functions \(\ell_s^k(y)=\alpha_s^k+(\beta_s^k)^{\mathsf T}y\) that are exact at \(y^k\). Add the single aggregate cut \(\theta\ge\sum_{s=1}^S\ell_s^k(y)\). Stop when the incumbent upper bound minus the master lower bound is at most \(\varepsilon\); otherwise repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each iteration aggregates all component certificates into one master inequality and stops when the certified optimality gap meets tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\) is the master feasible set and each \(v_s\) is bounded below on relevant points.
Each generated \(\ell_s^k\) satisfies \(\ell_s^k(y)\le v_s(y)\) for all \(y\in Y\).
Subproblem solutions provide certificates exact at \(y^k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta\ge\sum_{s=1}^S\ell_s^k(y)\) is added as one valid aggregate cut per iteration.

notation.meaning: indices of aggregate cuts before iteration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but the empty initial cut set leaves theta unbounded unless an initial lower bound is imposed. A source is needed for the precise single-cut generalized Benders formulation and stopping conditions.

children.title: Multicut Generalized Benders
children.top_down_role: Projected-master architectures retaining disaggregated subproblem information.

knowledge_statements.title: Multicut Generalized Benders
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise-cut variant for a separable convex subproblem value function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v(y)=\sum_{s=1}^S v_s(y)\) on \(Y\), and introduce \(\theta_s\) for each component. At iteration \(k\), solve \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}y+\sum_s\theta_s:y\in Y,\ \theta_s\ge\ell_s^j(y),\ s=1,\ldots,S,\ j<k\}\), obtaining \(y^k\). For every component, solve its convex subproblem and construct a valid lower function \(\ell_s^k(y)=\alpha_s^k+(\beta_s^k)^{\mathsf T}y\) exact at \(y^k\). Add all \(S\) cuts \(\theta_s\ge\ell_s^k(y)\). Stop when the incumbent upper bound and master lower bound differ by at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each iteration adds a separate cut and value variable for every separable subproblem component.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\) is the master feasible set and the value function separates as \(v=\sum_s v_s\).
Each \(\ell_s^k\) globally underestimates \(v_s\) on \(Y\).
Each component certificate is exact at the evaluated point \(y^k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta_s\ge\ell_s^k(y)\) is added separately for every \(s\).

notation.meaning: component lower certificate generated at iteration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but the initial master is unbounded in the component value variables unless valid initial lower bounds are supplied. The exact multicut formulation and termination claim require a source.

children.title: Cut-Granularity Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Master strength, cut volume, plus subproblem separability across aggregation choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Granularity Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Master-strength comparison between aggregate and componentwise Benders cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix component lower functions \(\ell_s^j\) and identify the aggregate variable by \(\theta=\sum_{s=1}^S\theta_s\). The multicut system \(\theta_s\ge\ell_s^j(y)\) for every \(s,j\) implies every same-iteration aggregate inequality \(\theta\ge\sum_s\ell_s^j(y)\). Thus its projection into \((y,\theta)\)-space is contained in the corresponding single-cut relaxation. The containment can be strict because componentwise cuts may combine indices \(j_s\) independently. Multicut masters therefore give bounds at least as strong, while using more variables and inequalities per iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For identical component certificates, the multicut master projects inside the single-cut master, but requires more master rows and auxiliary variables.
assumptions_latex: Both formulations use the same collection of valid component lower functions.
The aggregate variable satisfies \(\theta=\sum_s\theta_s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_{y,\theta}(M_{\mathrm{multi}})\subseteq M_{\mathrm{single}}\), with possible strict containment.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind and projection-containment comparison are mathematically plausible, but the record supplies no source for the multicut dominance and strict-containment claims.

children.title: Stabilized Generalized Benders
children.top_down_role: Regularized projected-master variants.

knowledge_statements.title: Stabilized Generalized Benders
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal stabilization of the projected generalized Benders master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a master center \(\bar y^k\), parameter \(\rho_k>0\), and accumulated valid cuts \(\theta\ge\ell_j(y)\), compute \((y^k,\theta^k)\) from \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}y+\theta+(\rho_k/2)\lVert y-\bar y^k\rVert_2^2:y\in Y,\ \theta\ge\ell_j(y)\}\). Solve the convex subproblem at \(y^k\), add an exact valid cut \(\ell_k\), and update an incumbent upper bound. Set \(\bar y^{k+1}=y^k\) after a prescribed sufficient-improvement test; otherwise retain \(\bar y^{k+1}=\bar y^k\). Stop when the unstabilized valid lower bound and incumbent upper bound differ by at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal term restrains master movement around a center, while valid cuts and unstabilized bounds retain the convergence certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\) is a nonempty mixed-integer master set.
Every \(\ell_j\) is a global lower bound for the projected value function.
\(\rho_k>0\), and stabilization is excluded from the reported global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((y^k,\theta^k)\) minimizes the stabilized master, while termination uses valid unstabilized bounds.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind matches the stabilized-variant topic, but the sufficient-improvement test is unspecified and no source supports this particular proximal master, center update, or termination certificate.

children.title: Logic-Based Benders Boundary
children.top_down_role: Interface with inference-based decomposition when convex dual certificates are unavailable.

knowledge_statements.title: Logic-Based Benders Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between multiplier-certified and inference-certified Benders decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed master assignment \(\bar y\), classical generalized Benders requires a convex subproblem certificate producing a globally valid inequality \(\ell(y)\le v(y)\), normally from strong Lagrangian duality and attained multipliers. If the subproblem is discrete or nonconvex and no such multiplier certificate is valid and exact, that construction is unavailable. Logic-based Benders instead requires a sound inference certificate \(I_{\bar y}\) yielding a master constraint \(C_{\bar y}(y)\) that excludes \(\bar y\) or bounds its value without excluding any assignment extendable to a better feasible solution. This certificate is not justified merely by convex duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When convex dual multipliers cannot certify a subproblem, valid decomposition requires problem-specific logical inference rather than a generalized Benders cut.
assumptions_latex: \(v(y)\) is the value of the subproblem induced by master assignment \(y\).
No attained convex-dual certificate exact at \(\bar y\) is available.
The inference system used for logic-based cuts is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{absence of a dual certificate}\Longrightarrow\text{a valid cut requires an independent inference certificate}\).

notation.meaning: master constraint derived from the inference certificate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the terminal context, but the transition from unavailable convex-dual certificates to logic-based inference needs a specific logic-based Benders source and a precise account of valid inference cuts.

children.title: Extended-Projected Cut Representation Pair

children.title: Extended-Space Cuts
children.top_down_role: Support information retained in spaces containing original plus auxiliary variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Extended-Space Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Valid inequalities retaining continuous subproblem variables in an extended formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E=\{(y,x,\eta)\in Y\times X\times\mathbb R:g(x,y)\le0,\ \eta\ge f(x,y)\}\). An extended-space cut is an inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}y+b^{\mathsf T}x+c\eta\ge d\) that is valid for \(E\), meaning it holds for every \((y,x,\eta)\in E\). It is separating for a candidate \((\bar y,\bar x,\bar\eta)\) when \(a^{\mathsf T}\bar y+b^{\mathsf T}\bar x+c\bar\eta<d\). Because \(x\) remains explicit, the cut need not itself be expressible solely in the projected master variables \((y,\eta)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extended-space cut is a valid separating inequality involving both master variables and retained continuous subproblem variables.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) and \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
\(E\) is the stated extended epigraph feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^{\mathsf T}y+b^{\mathsf T}x+c\eta\ge d\quad\forall (y,x,\eta)\in E\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits, but f and g and their codomains are not introduced in the statement or assumptions, and no source supports the intended extended-space terminology in this separation context.

children.title: Projected-Space Cuts
children.top_down_role: Support information expressed after eliminating continuous or auxiliary variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected-Space Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Valid inequalities expressed only in projected master and epigraph variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the extended feasible set \(E\subseteq\mathbb R^p\times\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\), define \(P=\operatorname{proj}_{y,\eta}(E)=\{(y,\eta):\exists x\text{ with }(y,x,\eta)\in E\}\). A projected-space cut is an inequality \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}y+\gamma\eta\ge\beta\) valid for every \((y,\eta)\in P\). It separates a candidate \((\bar y,\bar\eta)\) when \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}\bar y+\gamma\bar\eta<\beta\). Equivalently, its lifting with zero coefficient on \(x\) is valid for \(E\), so it can be imposed directly in a master formulation containing only \((y,\eta)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projected-space cut is a valid separating inequality in master and epigraph variables, with continuous subproblem variables eliminated.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a nonempty extended feasible set.
\(P=\operatorname{proj}_{y,\eta}(E)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}y+\gamma\eta\ge\beta\quad\forall (y,\eta)\in P\).

notation.meaning: projection of the extended set into master space

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is internally coherent and the content kind fits, but no cited source supports the projected-space cut terminology or its role in the stated extended-projected representation pair.

children.title: Projection Strength Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Comparisons of master compactness, certificate cost, plus information loss under projection.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection Strength Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact projection preserves relaxation strength but may enlarge explicit cut descriptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be a closed convex extended relaxation and \(P=\operatorname{proj}_{y,\eta}(E)\). Optimizing any linear objective depending only on \((y,\eta)\) over \(E\) gives the same bound as optimizing it over \(P\). If a projected master uses only a collection \(H\) of valid inequalities and defines \(P_H\supseteq P\), its bound is no stronger than the exact projected bound, with equality precisely when the relevant optimum over \(P_H\) is attained in \(P\). Thus projection causes no intrinsic strength loss, but an incomplete projected-cut description can be weaker while a compact extended formulation may retain exactness with auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact projection preserves bounds; weakness arises from using only some projected cuts, while extended formulations may encode the same set more compactly.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a nonempty closed convex relaxation.
The optimized linear objective depends only on \((y,\eta)\).
\(P_H\) is defined by valid projected inequalities and contains \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{(y,x,\eta)\in E}q^{\mathsf T}y+r\eta=\inf_{(y,\eta)\in P}q^{\mathsf T}y+r\eta\ge\inf_{(y,\eta)\in P_H}q^{\mathsf T}y+r\eta\).

notation.meaning: exact projection of the extended relaxation
outer approximation formed from selected projected cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits and exact projection preserves objective infima, but the stated 'precisely when' characterization overlooks equality without attainment. A source and a corrected attainment-qualified formulation are required.

children.title: Subproblem-Centered Separation
children.top_down_role: Refinement information obtained from fixed-integer convex subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Subproblem-Centered Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized-Benders separation obtained from a primal-dual solution of the convex continuous subproblem at a fixed discrete assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(Y\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) be nonempty convex sets, let \(Y_I\subseteq Y\) be the admissible discrete assignments, and let \(m\in\mathbb N\). Define \(v(y)=\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x,y):g_i(x,y)\le0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\). At \(\bar y\in Y_I\), obtain a primal-dual saddle point \((\bar x,\bar\lambda)\), where \(\bar\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\), for \(L(x,y,\lambda)=f(x,y)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i g_i(x,y)\). For any \(s\in\partial_y L(\bar x,\bar y,\bar\lambda)\), add \(\theta\ge v(\bar y)+s^{\mathsf T}(y-\bar y)\) to the projected master. Joint convexity and the saddle-point conditions make this inequality valid for every \(y\in Y\), and it is tight at \(\bar y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the continuous convex subproblem at a fixed discrete assignment and use a primal-dual saddle point to generate a globally valid value-function support cut that is tight at that assignment.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(Y\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) are nonempty and convex, with \(Y_I\subseteq Y\).
\(f:X\times Y\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) and \(g_i:X\times Y\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) are proper jointly convex functions.
The subproblem at \(\bar y\in Y_I\) attains its optimum and admits the stated primal-dual saddle point.
The partial subdifferential \(\partial_y L(\bar x,\bar y,\bar\lambda)\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta\ge v(\bar y)+s^{\mathsf T}(y-\bar y)\) is valid for all \(y\in Y\) and holds with equality at \(y=\bar y\).

notation.meaning: optimal value of the continuous subproblem at parameter y

children.title: Relaxation-Point Separation
children.top_down_role: Refinement information generated from violated nonlinear structure at relaxation solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Point Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer-approximation separation performed directly at a point returned by the current master relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+p}\) be convex, write \(z=(x,y)\in D\), and let \((\hat z,\hat\theta)\in D\times\mathbb R\) solve the current relaxation. For each differentiable convex constraint \(g_i:D\to\mathbb R\) with \(g_i(\hat z)>0\), add \(g_i(\hat z)+\nabla g_i(\hat z)^{\mathsf T}(z-\hat z)\le0\). For a differentiable convex objective \(f:D\to\mathbb R\), if \(\hat\theta<f(\hat z)\), add \(\theta\ge f(\hat z)+\nabla f(\hat z)^{\mathsf T}(z-\hat z)\). Every added inequality is globally valid on \(D\), and each inequality selected by its stated violation test excludes \((\hat z,\hat\theta)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the current relaxation point, linearize each violated convex constraint and any violated objective epigraph; the resulting globally valid support cuts exclude that point.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+p}\) is convex and contains \(\hat z\).
\(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m:D\to\mathbb R\) are differentiable and convex.
At least one nonlinear constraint or the objective epigraph is violated at \((\hat z,\hat\theta)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected affine supports are valid for the convex feasible epigraph and exclude \((\hat z,\hat\theta)\).

notation.meaning: combined continuous and relaxed-discrete variable vector

children.title: Separation-Source Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Comparisons involving cut strength, continuous-solve cost, plus refinement frequency.

knowledge_statements.title: Separation-Source Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of subproblem-centered and relaxation-point separation under a common convex MINLP master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed discrete point \(\bar y\), a solved convex subproblem can furnish a value-function support cut that is tight at \(\bar y\), but its generation requires an NLP solve and dual information. Separation at a relaxation point \((\hat x,\hat y)\) requires only function and subgradient evaluations and immediately removes that point, but need not reproduce the tight projected value-function support at \(\hat y\). Consequently, neither source uniformly dominates in both master strengthening and generation effort; dominance must be assessed using the resulting relaxation bound together with the cost of producing the certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subproblem cuts can be tighter at a discrete assignment but cost an NLP solve; point cuts are cheaper, yet may provide weaker projected information.
assumptions_latex: Both procedures generate globally valid cuts for the same convex MINLP epigraph.
Subproblem-centered separation satisfies the strong-duality conditions needed for its value-function cut.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No unconditional ordering holds simultaneously for cut strength and certificate-generation cost.

notation.meaning: fixed discrete assignment used by subproblem separation
point supplied by the current relaxation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The qualitative strength-versus-effort comparison fits the property leaf, but no source supports the asserted absence of uniform dominance or the relative generation costs.

children.title: OA–Generalized Benders Representation Relationships

knowledge_statements.title: OA–Generalized Benders Representation Relationships
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-space outer approximation and projected generalized-Benders descriptions of a convex subproblem value epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v(y)=\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x,y):g(x,y)\le0\}\). An exact extended outer-approximation description retains \(x\) and all valid supporting inequalities of the convex objective epigraph and constraints. Projecting this description onto \((y,\theta)\) yields \(\operatorname{epi}v=\{(y,\theta):\theta\ge v(y)\}\). Equivalently, for proper closed convex \(v\), \(\operatorname{epi}v=\bigcap_{\bar y\in\operatorname{dom}v,\ s\in\partial v(\bar y)}\{(y,\theta):\theta\ge v(\bar y)+s^{\mathsf T}(y-\bar y)\}\). Generalized-Benders cuts are these projected supports; finite OA and Benders masters are generally approximations and coincide only when their retained cuts induce the same projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete OA support information in extended variables projects to the value-function epigraph, whose supporting inequalities are generalized-Benders cuts.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is closed and convex, and the parametric subproblem has a proper closed convex value function \(v\).
Strong duality holds wherever multipliers are used to construct projected supports.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The complete OA extended formulation and the complete generalized-Benders cut family have the same projection onto \((y,\theta)\).

notation.meaning: convex subdifferential at the reference assignment

children.title: Master Relaxation Strength

knowledge_statements.title: Master Relaxation Strength
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Containment and bound ordering for valid master relaxations of one minimization problem over a fixed node domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), let \(F\subseteq Z\times\mathbb R\) be the feasible epigraph of a minimization problem, and let \(R_1,R_2\subseteq Z\times\mathbb R\) satisfy \(F\subseteq R_j\). Define \(L(R_j)=\inf\{\theta:(z,\theta)\in R_j\}\). The relaxation \(R_1\) is at least as strong as \(R_2\) in the containment sense when \(R_1\subseteq R_2\); this implies \(L(R_1)\ge L(R_2)\). It gives a strictly stronger bound at the current node when \(L(R_1)>L(R_2)\). This ordering does not compare solution costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid master relaxation is containment-stronger when it is a subset of another relaxation, which gives a no-smaller lower bound for the same minimization problem.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is the common node domain.
\(F\subseteq R_1\cap R_2\subseteq Z\times\mathbb R\).
Both relaxations minimize the same epigraph variable \(\theta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_1\subseteq R_2\Longrightarrow L(R_1)\ge L(R_2)\).

children.title: Certificate Generation Cost

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Generation Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work required to produce and validate one decomposition certificate under a declared computational model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a computational model with unit costs for oracle calls, derivative evaluations, linear-algebra operations, and optimization solves. For a certificate-generation procedure \(P\) and query \(q\), define \(C_P(q)\) as the resulting work vector, for example \(C_P(q)=(N_{\mathrm{NLP}},N_f,N_g,N_{\partial},T)\). Scalar cost is \(c_P(q)=w^{\mathsf T}C_P(q)\) for a declared nonnegative weight vector \(w\). Comparisons of certificate cost are meaningful only under the same oracle model, accuracy tolerances, warm-start convention, and accounting horizon; cut sparsity or master-solution time is separate unless explicitly included.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certificate cost records the declared solver, oracle, derivative, and time resources needed to generate and validate a cut or bound.
assumptions_latex: All compared procedures use the same accuracy, warm-start, and resource-accounting conventions.
The weight vector satisfies \(w\ge0\) when a scalar cost is reported.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c_P(q)=w^{\mathsf T}C_P(q)\) defines a comparable scalar certificate-generation cost under the fixed model.

notation.meaning: resource vector for procedure P on query q

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed resource-vector formalization is coherent and fits the definition leaf, but it is a nonstandard operational definition with no cited source establishing this particular accounting model.

children.title: Strength–Cost Frontier
children.top_down_role: Architectural regimes balancing stronger master information against certificate expense.

knowledge_statements.title: Strength–Cost Frontier
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pareto frontier of master-bound improvement and certificate-generation cost for a fixed node state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P\) be a family of valid certificate procedures. For \(P\in\mathcal P\), let \(S(P)=L(R_P)-L(R_0)\ge0\) be the lower-bound improvement obtained by adding its certificates to baseline master \(R_0\), and let \(C(P)\ge0\) be their generation cost. Procedure \(P\) dominates \(Q\) when \(S(P)\ge S(Q)\) and \(C(P)\le C(Q)\), with at least one strict inequality. The strength–cost frontier is the set of procedures not dominated by any member of \(\mathcal P\). Its membership depends on the node state, accuracy convention, and cost model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The frontier contains certificate procedures for which no alternative gives at least as much bound improvement at no greater generation cost.
assumptions_latex: Every \(R_P\) is a valid relaxation of the same minimization problem and node domain.
Strength and cost are measured from the same baseline and under fixed conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F=\{P\in\mathcal P:\nexists Q\in\mathcal P\text{ dominating }P\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Pareto definition is internally coherent and fits the leaf, but the specialized strength–cost measures and their frontier have no supporting citation.

children.title: Convex NLP Node Relaxations

knowledge_statements.title: Convex NLP Node Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous convex relaxation of a branch-and-bound node obtained by relaxing discrete restrictions within its local domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(N\), let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be convex, let \(Y_N\subseteq\mathbb Z^p\) be the node's permitted discrete assignments, and let \(\widehat Y_N\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) be a convex set containing \(Y_N\). Define \(L_N=\inf\{f(x,y):x\in X,\ y\in\widehat Y_N,\ g_i(x,y)\le0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) and \(z_N=\inf\{f(x,y):x\in X,\ y\in Y_N,\ g_i(x,y)\le0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\). If \(f\) and all \(g_i\) are convex on \(X\times\widehat Y_N\), the first problem is a convex NLP and satisfies \(L_N\le z_N\). If its feasible set is empty, then the mixed-integer feasible set at node \(N\) is also empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing a node's discrete domain by a containing convex domain yields a convex NLP lower bound, and infeasibility of that relaxation certifies node infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(\widehat Y_N\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) are convex.
\(Y_N\subseteq\widehat Y_N\) and \(Y_N\subseteq\mathbb Z^p\).
\(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\) are convex on \(X\times\widehat Y_N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_N\le z_N\), and infeasibility of the relaxation implies infeasibility of node \(N\).

notation.meaning: discrete assignments permitted at node N
convex continuous relaxation of the node's discrete domain
convex-NLP relaxation value at node N

children.title: NLP Branching Families
children.top_down_role: Branching mechanisms adapted to discrete variables and nonlinear relaxation behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: NLP Branching Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exhaustive, convexity-preserving branching rules for partitioning a convex-NLP node relaxation without losing mixed-integer solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a parent node \(N\) with relaxation solution \((\hat x,\hat y)\), choose disjuncts \(D_1,\ldots,D_k\) such that every mixed-integer feasible point of \(N\) satisfies at least one \(D_j\), and such that intersecting the parent relaxation with each \(D_j\) preserves convexity. If an integer-constrained component \(\hat y_i\) is fractional, standard integer branching uses \(y_i\le\lfloor\hat y_i\rfloor\) or \(y_i\ge\lceil\hat y_i\rceil\); binary branching uses \(y_i=0\) or \(y_i=1\). Create one child for each disjunct, retain the parent constraints and bounds, add that disjunct, and solve the resulting child convex-NLP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use an exhaustive disjunction whose individual branches preserve convexity—such as floor/ceiling or binary branching—then solve the convex NLP relaxation of each child.
assumptions_latex: The parent mixed-integer feasible set \(F_N\) is covered by \(D_1\cup\cdots\cup D_k\).
For every \(j\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\), adding \(D_j\) preserves convexity of the child relaxation.
Each child retains all parent restrictions and adds exactly its assigned disjunct.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_N=\bigcup_{j=1}^k F_{N,j}\), so processing all children preserves every parent mixed-integer feasible point.

notation.meaning: mixed-integer feasible set of the parent node
mixed-integer feasible set of child j

children.title: NLP Node-Processing Architecture
children.top_down_role: Coordination of relaxation solves, pruning, incumbents, and continuous-solver state.

knowledge_statements.title: NLP Node-Processing Architecture
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node workflow combining convex-NLP bounds, feasibility tests, incumbent updates, pruning, and branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an active node \(N\), solve its convex NLP relaxation to tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NLP}}\). If it is infeasible, prune \(N\). Otherwise obtain lower bound \(L_N\) and solution \((\hat x,\hat y)\). Given incumbent value \(U\), prune when \(L_N\ge U-\varepsilon\). If \(\hat y\) is discrete-feasible and the nonlinear constraints hold, update \(U\leftarrow\min\{U,f(\hat x,\hat y)\}\) and fathom when certified. Otherwise choose an exhaustive branching disjunction, create children, transfer only solver state valid for each child, and continue until no active node can improve \(U\) by more than \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each node is relaxed, bounded, pruned or used to update the incumbent, then branched if unresolved; termination certifies the requested global gap.
assumptions_latex: Each node relaxation supplies a certified lower bound within \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{NLP}}\).
Branching is exhaustive, and inherited solver information remains valid for each child.
The incumbent \(U\) is the value of a feasible mixed-integer point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When all active nodes satisfy \(L_N\ge U-\varepsilon\), the incumbent is globally \(\varepsilon\)-optimal.

notation.meaning: certified lower bound at node N

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The workflow fits the algorithm leaf, but the certified approximate-NLP bound convention, fathoming rule, solver-state transfer, and global termination certificate require a direct convex-MINLP branch-and-bound source.

children.title: LP Outer-Model Node Bounds
children.top_down_role: Tree bounds supplied by accumulated convex support information.

knowledge_statements.title: LP Outer-Model Node Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower bounds from finitely many globally valid affine supports accumulated in an LP node master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_N\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be the node domain described by linear restrictions, and let \(\mathcal C\) be a finite family of affine support cuts. For every sampled \(u\in D_N\), a constraint cut has the form \(g_i(u)+s_{iu}^{\mathsf T}(z-u)\le0\), where \(s_{iu}\in\partial g_i(u)\), and an objective cut has the form \(\theta\ge f(u)+t_u^{\mathsf T}(z-u)\), where \(t_u\in\partial f(u)\). Let \(L_N^{\mathrm{LP}}(\mathcal C)\) be the infimum of \(\theta\) over \(D_N\) and the cuts in \(\mathcal C\). Convexity makes every cut valid for every nonlinear-feasible point at the node, so \(L_N^{\mathrm{LP}}(\mathcal C)\le z_N\). If \(\mathcal C_1\subseteq\mathcal C_2\), then \(L_N^{\mathrm{LP}}(\mathcal C_1)\le L_N^{\mathrm{LP}}(\mathcal C_2)\).

If strong duality and the required saddle-point conditions hold, optimal multipliers can also generate a valid projected value cut. If the subproblem is infeasible, exclude \(\bar y\) only when a valid infeasibility certificate yields a corresponding feasibility cut; an unsuccessful solver return alone does not justify exclusion.

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Nonlinear-Cut Integration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Propagation of globally or locally valid convex support cuts through an active branch-and-bound tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing a convex differentiable objective \(f(z)\) subject to convex differentiable inequalities \(g_i(z)\le 0\), original domain restrictions, and any declared integrality restrictions. Install \(c\) in every open node \(v\) satisfying \(D_v\subseteq V_c\); globally valid cuts may therefore be installed in every open node. Reoptimize affected relaxations and prune a node only when the strengthened relaxation is certified infeasible or its certified lower bound meets the incumbent cutoff.

children.title: LP/NLP Bound Certificates

knowledge_statements.title: LP/NLP Bound Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node and global lower-bound certificates obtained from valid LP outer approximations or convex NLP relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem with feasible set \(F\), let node \(v\) have domain \(D_v\). A node bound certificate consists of a relaxation \(R_v\supseteq F\cap D_v\), a relaxation objective \(f_R\) satisfying \(f_R(z)\le f(z)\) for every \(z\in F\cap D_v\), and a certified value \(L_v\le\inf\{f_R(z):z\in R_v\}\). Then \(L_v\le f(z)\) for every \(z\in F\cap D_v\). An LP outer approximation supplies such a certificate when all its inequalities and objective underestimators are valid; a convex NLP relaxation does so under the analogous validity conditions. If \(U\) is a certified incumbent value and every feasible point either belongs to an active-leaf domain \(D_v\), with \(v\in\mathcal L\), or has objective value at least \(U\), then \(L=\min\bigl(\{U\}\cup\{L_v:v\in\mathcal L\}\bigr)\) is a certified global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rigorously bounded valid LP or convex NLP relaxation certifies a node lower bound. Combining active-leaf bounds with the incumbent value gives a global lower bound when active nodes and the incumbent cutoff account for every feasible point.
assumptions_latex: The original problem is a minimization problem with feasible set \(F\).
For each active node \(v\), the relaxation \(R_v\) contains \(F\cap D_v\), and its objective underestimates the original objective there.
Every feasible point outside the active-leaf domains has certified objective value at least the incumbent value \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every active node \(v\), \(L_v\le\inf_{z\in F\cap D_v}f(z)\), and \(L=\min\bigl(\{U\}\cup\{L_v:v\in\mathcal L\}\bigr)\le f^\star\).

It certifies \(f^\star\le U\) for a minimization problem. If the fixed-integer NLP is convex and solved globally, its optimizer also certifies the best objective attainable under \(y=\hat y\); global NLP optimality is not required merely to certify feasibility and an upper bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound–Incumbent Gap Certification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute and relative optimality certification for minimization using valid lower and incumbent upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\) be a certified global lower bound and let \(U\) be the objective value of a certified feasible incumbent for a minimization problem with finite optimum \(f^\star\). Then \(L\le f^\star\le U\), so \(G=U-L\ge0\) is a certified absolute optimality gap. For a chosen scale \(s>0\), \(G_{\mathrm{rel}}=(U-L)/\max\{s,|U|,|L|\}\) is a certified scaled relative gap. Termination with \(G\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\), or with \(G_{\mathrm{rel}}\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\), certifies the corresponding requested accuracy; \(U=L\) certifies global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid lower and incumbent upper bounds enclose the optimum; their difference or declared scaled ratio provides a checkable termination certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(L\le f^\star\le U\).
\(s>0\) and both accuracy tolerances are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le U-f^\star\le U-L\), with exact optimality certified when \(U=L\).

knowledge_statements.title: OA-to-Tree Switching

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Domain Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative contraction of variable domains using convex constraints and current node bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Start from a node box \(B^0=\prod_j[\ell_j^0,u_j^0]\). For each variable \(z_j\), compute valid bounds over the current convex relaxation \(R(B^k)\): \(\ell_j^{k+1}=\max\{\ell_j^k,\inf_{z\in R(B^k)}z_j\}\) and \(u_j^{k+1}=\min\{u_j^k,\sup_{z\in R(B^k)}z_j\}\). Apply sound constraint-specific implications, intersect all resulting intervals, and repeat until no bound changes beyond tolerance. If any lower bound exceeds its upper bound, certify the node relaxation infeasible; otherwise output the contracted box, which still contains every feasible point of the original node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly optimize or infer each variable's bounds over a convex node relaxation, intersect domains, and detect empty intervals without removing feasible points.

All subproblem bounds and constraint implications are valid.

children.title: Convex Bound Tightening

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Bound Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization-based variable-bound tightening over a convex node relaxation, optionally restricted to potentially improving solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a node relaxation \(R_v\) and each selected variable \(z_j\), compute rigorous values or outward-safe bounds for \(L_j=\inf\{z_j:z\in R_v\}\) and \(U_j=\sup\{z_j:z\in R_v\}\), solving the upper-bound problem by minimizing \(-z_j\). Replace the current interval \([\ell_j,u_j]\) by \([\max\{\ell_j,L_j\},\min\{u_j,U_j\}]\). If \(R_v\) is certified infeasible, the node is infeasible. For improvement-oriented tightening, one may instead use a valid convex set \(R_v^{\mathrm{cut}}=R_v\cap\{z:f_R(z)\le U^{\mathrm{inc}}-\delta\}\), where \(f_R\) is a valid convex objective representation and \(\delta\ge0\) is the declared improvement margin. Infeasibility of \(R_v^{\mathrm{cut}}\) certifies that the node contains no solution meeting that improvement cutoff, but does not by itself certify infeasibility of the original node.

Reported optimization bounds are rigorous or rounded outward.
When used, \(f_R(z)\le U^{\mathrm{inc}}-\delta\) is a valid convex restriction defining the solutions relevant to the declared improvement margin \(\delta\ge0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete–Convex Inference Coupling

Conversely, if the convex relaxation under a discrete literal \(a\) is infeasible, infer the valid clause \(\neg a\); if optimizing over that relaxation yields valid variable bounds, return those bounds to discrete propagation. children.title: Discrete Symmetry Control

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete Symmetry Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical-orbit filtering for permutation symmetries of bounded integer variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a finite group \(G\) act by coordinate permutations on the discrete domain \(Y\subseteq\mathbb Z^p\), and assume the objective and feasible set are \(G\)-invariant. Fix a total order \(\preceq\) on \(Y\). Initialize the search with the canonicality rule \(y=\min_{\preceq}\{g y:g\in G\}\). At each node, discard any partial assignment for which a group element produces a strictly smaller compatible assignment; otherwise branch normally. Stop when every surviving node is fathomed. Return the best feasible solution found. Every orbit retains a representative, so canonical filtering preserves the global optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search only canonical representatives of symmetry orbits; invariance ensures that this removes redundant assignments without removing every optimum.

The objective and feasible region are invariant under every \(g\in G\).
The canonicality test is exact for each discarded assignment.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Redundancy Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate-based suppression of nonlinear constraints already implied by the active relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_k\) be the current convex relaxation and let \(h(x,y)\leq0\) be a proposed valid nonlinear constraint. Initialize the stored family as \(H_0=\varnothing\). Before adding \(h\), solve or otherwise certify the redundancy test \(\sup\{h(x,y):(x,y)\in R_k\}\leq0\). If certified, reject \(h\); otherwise add it to \(H_k\), update \(R_k\), and optionally delete any stored constraint whose redundancy is subsequently certified. Stop when no proposed constraint violates the test tolerance. The resulting relaxation has the same feasible set as adding every rejected constraint.

Each redundancy test supplies a rigorous global upper bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Induced Cut Duplication
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orbit equivalence and canonical storage of cuts under discrete symmetries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times Y\) be invariant under a finite linear symmetry group \(G\). If \(c(z)=a^{\mathsf T}z-b\leq0\) is valid for \(F\), then for every \(g\in G\), the transported inequality \(c_g(z)=a^{\mathsf T}g^{-1}z-b\leq0\) is also valid. These inequalities form the cut orbit \(Gc\); adding separately generated members of the same orbit duplicates symmetry-equivalent information. A canonical signature constant on \(Gc\) permits storage of one representative without losing validity, while all orbit members can be regenerated when required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid cut generates an orbit of valid symmetry-equivalent cuts; canonical orbit signatures prevent duplicate storage.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and acts linearly on the model variables.
The feasible region satisfies \(gF=F\) for every \(g\in G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c(z)\leq0\text{ valid on }F\ \Longrightarrow\ c_g(z)=c(g^{-1}z)\leq0\text{ valid on }F\quad(\forall g\in G).\)

children.title: Convex Feasibility-Restoration Families

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Feasibility-Restoration Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Slack-minimization restoration model for a fixed discrete assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed assignment \(\bar y\), let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and convex and let each \(g_i(\cdot,\bar y)\) be convex. Choose weights \(w_i>0\) and solve the restoration problem \[\rho(\bar y)=\min_{x\in X,\ s\in\mathbb R_+^m}\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m w_i s_i:g_i(x,\bar y)\leq s_i\ (i=1,\ldots,m)\right\}.\] If an optimum is attained, output a feasible point when \(\rho(\bar y)=0\), and declare the fixed assignment infeasible when \(\rho(\bar y)>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize weighted nonnegative constraint violations at a fixed integer assignment; zero optimum gives feasibility, while a positive attained optimum proves infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is closed and convex, and every \(g_i(\cdot,\bar y)\) is convex.
All restoration weights satisfy \(w_i>0\).
The restoration optimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho(\bar y)=0\iff\exists x\in X:\ g_i(x,\bar y)\leq0\ (i=1,\ldots,m).\)

children.title: Dual Infeasibility Certificates

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrangian certificate for infeasibility of a fixed-integer convex subsystem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(\bar y\) and consider \(g_i(x,\bar y)\leq0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\) over a nonempty convex set \(X\). A vector \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\) satisfying \[\delta:=\inf_{x\in X}\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i g_i(x,\bar y)>0\] is a verifiable infeasibility certificate. Indeed, any feasible \(x\) would make every weighted term sum to a nonpositive value, contradicting the certified positive lower bound \(\delta\). Thus the assignment \(\bar y\) admits no feasible continuous completion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative multiplier vector whose weighted constraint sum has a positive global lower bound certifies infeasibility of the fixed assignment.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty and convex.
Each \(g_i(\cdot,\bar y)\) is real-valued and convex on \(X\).
The displayed infimum has a rigorously certified positive lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda\geq0,\ \inf_{x\in X}\sum_i\lambda_i g_i(x,\bar y)>0\ \Longrightarrow\ \nexists x\in X:\ g_i(x,\bar y)\leq0\ \forall i.\)

notation.meaning: certified positive lower bound on the weighted constraint sum

children.title: Integer-Assignment Exclusion

knowledge_statements.title: Integer-Assignment Exclusion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary no-good inequality excluding one certified infeasible assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y\in\{0,1\}^p\), and let \(\bar y\in\{0,1\}^p\) be an assignment whose continuous subproblem has been certified infeasible. Define \(I_1=\{j:\bar y_j=1\}\) and \(I_0=\{j:\bar y_j=0\}\). The no-good inequality \[\sum_{j\in I_1}(1-y_j)+\sum_{j\in I_0}y_j\geq1\] is violated exactly by \(y=\bar y\) and satisfied by every other binary assignment. Adding it therefore excludes the certified assignment without removing any distinct assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After proving a binary assignment infeasible, a no-good inequality excludes exactly that assignment and preserves all other binary vectors.
assumptions_latex: The discrete variables are binary.
The continuous subproblem at \(\bar y\) is rigorously certified infeasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y\in\{0,1\}^p\text{ satisfies the no-good inequality}\iff y\neq\bar y.\)

notation.meaning: indices equal to one in the excluded assignment
indices equal to zero in the excluded assignment

children.title: Continuous-Relaxation Bounds
